MESSAGE: Cholera is a disease caused by the bacterium Vibro Cholerae. It is spread by drinking infected water, which is usually contaminated with feces of infected people.
Symptoms of cholera include watery diarrhea, vomiting, and leg cramps. These lead to rapid water loss resulting in dehydration.

Cholera originated in India, and the first pandemic started in 1817 when trade routes from India to other asian countries spread the disease to parts of China, Japan, southern Russia, and other asian countries.

The second pandemic started in 1826, when it spread to North America, Europe and Egypt. In the third cholera pandemic, it spread to South America and wreaked havoc all over the world, including killing over a million people in Russia.
There were 3 more pandemics, killing millions and devastating the entire world. It stopped until the 1960s when the seventh cholera pandemic started, and we’re still in it today.

The World Health Organization has numerous programs to stop the spread of cholera, most of which are related to working with governments to implement surveillance, vaccinations, water cleaning, and more.
Cholera is a very serious problem for developing countries because it kills very quickly if untreated, and spreads quickly in communities with little access to clean water
